passage: Harsha, you asked why I'm up till midnight, so here it is. I'm Uday. I found this speaker online in the summer, and his videos make life feel clear. He talks about waking early, being kind, having a purpose, and for the first time I feel like someone explains why I get up. I've watched every video, some twice. Last week you sent me a talk by a different speaker on the same idea, and they disagreed on one point. That bothered me at first, then I liked it. Now I keep a note of what each video asks me to do: wake early, help at home, nothing about money. I still like him. I just compare now.

qa.q: When did Uday find the speaker online?
qa.a: Uday found the speaker in the summer.

qa.q: What is Uday feeling about the speaker, and what shows it?
qa.a: Uday admires the speaker; watching every video, some twice, and feeling that life is clear show it. 🙂

qa.q: What is the benefit of Uday's habit of noting what each video asks?
qa.a: It lets Uday compare speakers and see what is being asked, such as habits and not money, so enjoying the videos does not turn into blind following.

qa.q: How might Harsha see Uday's late nights and the different talk Harsha sent?
qa.a: Harsha probably cares and wanted Uday to hear another view, and Uday's reaction shows Harsha's suggestion was welcome.

grounding: Uday admires an online speaker who makes life feel clear, and enjoys the videos while comparing sources and noting what they ask.

passage:
Every evening at his father's hardware shop in Gadag, between customers, Lokesh watched the Swamiji videos on his phone. The man spoke so calmly about purpose and discipline that Lokesh felt, for the first time, that his life had a shape.

He started waking early, sweeping the shop before school without being asked. His father noticed and smiled.

Madhav, his friend from the bus, sat on the shop step one evening and asked, "Is he the one who says phones are poison? While being on your phone?"

Lokesh laughed. "He says a lot of things."

That night, though, he wrote them down. Wake early, be honest, respect parents: good. Tell ten people. Donate to the ashram before full moon. Don't read other teachers, they'll confuse you.

The last one bothered him. The next day he borrowed a book on the Gita from the school library and asked his Kannada teacher what she thought. He kept the early mornings. He stopped at the donation part.

qa.q: Where did Lokesh watch the videos?
qa.a: Lokesh watched them at his father's hardware shop in Gadag.

qa.q: What did Lokesh feel while watching the Swamiji videos?
qa.a: Lokesh felt inspired and calm, as if his life finally had a shape and purpose.

qa.q: What did Lokesh do that was wise?
qa.a: Lokesh wrote down what the speaker asked, noticed the warning sign of not reading other teachers, and checked with a library book and his teacher while keeping the good habits.

qa.q: How might Madhav see Lokesh's new routine?
qa.a: Madhav seems amused and a little doubtful about the speaker, but may also notice that Lokesh has become more disciplined.

grounding: It shows a teen who admires a charismatic online speaker, enjoys what helps, and compares with other sources while noting what the speaker asks of him.
